events.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern and eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and
Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow
accumulations between 10 and 18 inches, mainly above 8000 feet in
elevation. Winds gusting as high as 65 mph.

* WHERE...Snowy Range.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Outdoor recreation could become life threatening to those
caught unprepared for severe winter conditions. Hikers and
snowmobilers may easily become disoriented. Frostbite and
hypothermia can develop quickly. Widespread blowing snow could
significantly reduce visibility and lead to dangerous travel
conditions.

inches, mainly above 8000 feet. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Madre Range.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Extreme Western Allegany; Western Garrett; Eastern Garrett; Western Highland; Western Mineral
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Light snow will mix with patchy freezing drizzle over the higher
ridges through daybreak. Additional snow accumulations will be
less than an inch, but ice accumulations of a light glaze are
possible on the higher ridges.

Any untreated surface may be slippery, especially bridges and
overpasses. Please use extra caution when travelling late tonight
through this morning.
